We propose the following changes to the base model that was reviewed in August, 2025: 

<!-- These are quite short now. I meant them as placeholders, but I am envisioning each bullet could be much longer and include both motivation and additional detail -->

1. **Use the updated Washington historical catch reconstruction**
    a. GFSC Request 7 was to include this in a new base model. It has relatively little impact on the model results but represents the best scientific information available.

1. **Simplify the fleet structure:** The 2015 benchmark assessment model (and subsequent 2019 and 2025 updated assessment models) have a complex fleet structure, with multiple fleets contributing minimal amounts of catch (such as net and hook and line fleets) primarily in historical periods, with limited amount of length composition data available to reliably estimate associated selectivity curves. Also, for several fleets, discarding is estimated within the model, with retention curves informed by minimal amount of biological data. During the assessment process, it was discovered that limited discard length data for the hook-and-line fleet (which contributes less than half of a percent of recent catches) had a disproportionately high influence on recruitment estimates (not supported by any other sources). For the supplemental review, we therefore explored multiple model configurations with simplified fleet structures and arrive to the structure described below.

    a. The small amount of catches from fixed gear fleets (hook-and-line and net) was combined with the bottom trawl fleet, and their composition data were removed. In addition, the catches  made by the foreign hisrotical fishery targeting Pacific Ocean perch (1966-1976), were moved from the hake fleet to bottom trawl, as well.
        i. GFSC Requests 1 (reduce influence of hook-and-line composition data) and 6 (leave-one-out analysis) indicated that data from the smaller fleets have little influence on the model results;
        i. These fleets represent only 1.1% and 1.4% of the catch and are less likely to be representative of the population as a whole; 
        i. The issues with the hook-and-line discard length data resolved prior to the August 2025 base model showed that even small amounts of data from these fleets can have undue influence on the results when combined with mismatching assumptions for selectivity and retention.

1. **Use external estimates of discards rather than estimate within the model**.
    a. The use of estimated retention functions within the model was standard practice in 2015, following a long period of large discards due to trip limits. However, discard rates have been low for widow rockfish for more than 10 years so the benefit of using retention functions to extrapolate beyond the range of observed data is reduced and the biological data from the discards are no longer as likely to be informative about dynamics of the total population.
    a. Methods: 
        i. For the years 1982-1989, landings in the bottom trawl and midwater trawl fleets were scaled using fleet-specific discard rates estimated from the Pikitch
        i. For the years 1990-2001, landings in the bottom trawl and midwater trawl fleets were scaled using fleet-specific discard rates estimated from the EDCP data
        i. for the years 2002-2023, GEMM estimates of fleet-specific dicards amounts were added to the landed catch (bottom trawl + other, and midwater trawl)
        i. The 2024 values were set to the average from the GEMM estimates for the period 2021--2023. All retention parameters were removed from the model
        i. Total catch in the at-sea hake fishery was fully accounted for in the August 2025 base model and was not changed.

1. **The data weighting was updated.** The data weighting approach was changed to match recent practices, including the use of the Francis rather than McAllister-Ianelli approach, and no longer including a 50% additional reduction in weights.
    a. Data weighting remains a topic of ongoing research in the stock assessment community. However, the Francis method performed better in a simulation analysis (TODO: CITE PUNT PAPER) and has been the preferred approach in most recent stock assessments.  
    a. The 50% multplier on the data weights used in the previous assessment was an approach more common in 2015 to account for the potential double use of data since length and age are observed from the same fish. However, the sum of the adjusted input sample sizes for length and age data combined are already far lower than the number of number of sampled fish because they are primarily based on trips or hauls and then further reduced by the data-weigthing algorithm. This 50% adjustment is no longer common practice and has not been used any other recent assessments. 

1. **Change the selectivity blocking for the midwater trawl fleet.** The block that previously went from 2002 to 2010 was extended to 2016.
    a. The midwater trawl fleet has several blocks on selectivity, to account for changes in selectivity in 1983, when trip limits were introduced, and in 2002, when stock was declared overfished. It also had a block in 2011, associated with the start of the IFQ fishery. The most recent large removals of the widow rockfish by the shorebased midwater trawl fleet targeting rockfish started in 2017, a few years after widow rockfish was declared rebuilt. We explored multiple assumptions regarding blocks in the period of the recent fishery, starting with placing an additional block for 2017 forward. With that, we found that estimated selectivity curves for 2002-2010 and 2010-2016 periods were virtually identical, and therefore, removed a break associated with the start of the IFQ, extending the original block from 2002 to 2010 to go from 2002 to 2016. 

1. **Use a fecundity relationship rather than assume the number of eggs is proportional to body weight**
    a. As noted in GFSC Request 13, accounting for size-dependent fecundity in rockfish stocks using the meta-analysis from Dick et al. (2017) (TODO: ADD CITATION) has become standard practice in recent years and is included in the TOR and Accepted Practices Guidelines documents.
    a. Following standard practice for species that were not included in the meta-analyis, the predictive distributions for unobserved _Sebastes_ species was used. This relationship has the number of eggs proportional to length to the power 4.043 (as opposed to body weight which was estimated as proportional to length to the power 2.99) 

1. **Update bias adjustment using estimated values (modified to have full bias adjustment starting in 1970)**
    a. The data weighting changed the uncertainty around estimates of recent recruitment, necessitating a change in the recruitment bias adjustment settings. However, the estimated algorithm in the r4ss package continued to under-adjust the well-informed recruitments in 1970 and 1971 (see GFSC Request 5), so the inputs were modified to ensure full bias adjustment of the recruitments from 1970 onward.
